newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Fed fines Taiwan bank, orders divestiture.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fed fines Taiwan bank, orders divestiture.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Reserve on Friday said it ordered the International Commercial Bank of China to pay a $5.0 million fine for improper filings related to its takeover of a U.S. bank.
It also ordered the Taiwan-based bank to turn over $17.32 million of profits from the takeover of the Chinese American Bank of New York and to divest itself of the business.

Regulators said International Commercial Bank failed to file a complete application when it acquired Chinese American Bank and that it failed to file accurate reports fully and correctly with the Federal Reserve.

The Fed said its order did "not relate in any manner to the condition or activities of the Chinese American Bank, and the divestiture of the bank by the International Commercial Bank of China should not affect the bank's operations."
The Fed did not provide any details of how International Commercial Bank of China failed to meet filing requirements.
It said the Taiwanese bank had agreed to submit within 30 days a plan to the New York Fed on how it would divest itself of Chinese American Bank.
